audit_findings.title: Revo creates an unresolved perimeter break
audit_findings.mechanism: The 2025 OE anchor includes Revo fees through the third quarter, while the forward business excludes Revo fee recognition, excludes its rooms from growth guidance, and includes two foreclosed hotels plus possible collateral recoveries.
audit_findings.evidence: Such insolvency proceeding may not be resolved for several years and thus we are subject to uncertainty with respect to the value of our collateral and any potential recovery we may receive, as well as the ongoing viability of our franchise agreements and related loss of rooms and any future revenues.
audit_findings.explanation: The perimeter mismatch is demonstrated, but the filings do not isolate the recurring Revo fees embedded in the $175.3 million anchor. The latest filing identifies 19,800 Revo-related rooms, $23 million of acquired net hotel assets, $1 million of remaining receivables and $20 million of restricted cash subject to adjudication. These establish several opposing valuation effects but not their combined materiality.
audit_findings.action: Rerun OE using a 2026 run-rate that excludes all deferred Revo fees and terminated rooms, includes recurring income and required capital for the two owned hotels, and places the $20 million restricted cash and any other recoveries in a separate probability-weighted bridge item.

audit_findings.title: Advance payments may inflate the cash-flow anchor
audit_findings.magnitude: $62 million operating-cash-flow inflow, equal to 35.4% of the $175.3 million anchor; full removal would reduce computed base value by approximately $11.41 per share
audit_findings.mechanism: An increase in deferred revenue raises operating cash flow without representing services earned during the period; capitalizing that increase in OE raises every forecast year and terminal value.
audit_findings.evidence: Deferred revenues, or contract liabilities, generally represent payments or consideration received in advance for goods or services that the Company has not yet provided to the customer.
audit_findings.explanation: The $62 million cash-flow contribution is demonstrated, but its inclusion without normalization is unresolved. Its scale is plainly material: a full adjustment would remove more than one-third of the anchor and materially lower the $33.18 base valuation. Future fulfillment costs must remain even if the advance receipt is removed.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile the $175.3 million anchor to the cash-flow statement, remove the non-recurring portion of the 2025 deferred-revenue increase, retain associated fulfillment and redemption costs, and rerun all scenarios and the buy-below price.

audit_findings.title: Recurring franchisee financing may be outside owner earnings
audit_findings.magnitude: $57 million of net loan funding, equal to 32.5% of the anchor; $105 million of net development advances was already reported within operating cash flow
audit_findings.mechanism: Required franchisee funding is capital needed to obtain or preserve the growth projected in OE. Loan advances classified as investing cash flow may be omitted when OE is derived primarily from operating cash flow, while credit losses reduce the realizable repayments.
audit_findings.evidence: We allocated $57 million on loans, net of repayments, to franchisees during 2025 to support hotel development activities.
audit_findings.explanation: The classification issue is demonstrated for the $57 million of net loans, but whether the valuation deducted it is unresolved. The $105 million of development advances should already enter an operating-cash-flow-based calculation. Treating the $57 million as entirely recoverable while using the resulting system growth could materially overstate value, although the proper adjustment is the recurring economic funding cost after supportable repayments and recoveries—not necessarily the entire advance.
audit_findings.action: Trace both funding categories through the OE worksheet, establish normalized annual originations, repayments and credit losses from filed history, deduct the resulting recurring net investment, and rerun growth scenarios consistently.

audit_findings.title: A non-operating guarantee claim is absent from the equity bridge
audit_findings.magnitude: $20 million net claim ($61 million liability less $41 million receivable), equal to $0.26 per share and 0.8% of the $2.532 billion base equity value; gross-liability stress is $0.80 per share
audit_findings.mechanism: Because the guarantee is a non-operating claim without corresponding recurring interest in OE, its net expected amount belongs in the equity bridge.
audit_findings.evidence: The fair value of the guarantees was $ 61 million as of December 31, 2025 and 2024 and was included in other non-current liabilities on the Consolidated Balance Sheets.
audit_findings.explanation: The bridge omission is demonstrated, but the filed scale is not capable of changing the valuation conclusion. Even assuming the entire $41 million receivable is uncollectible, the $61 million gross claim is only 2.4% of base equity value and would reduce base value by about $0.80 per share.
audit_findings.action: Confirm the guarantee and former-parent receivable remain outstanding at the valuation date, then rerun the bridge using a $20 million net deduction and a $61 million gross-liability stress case.

audit_findings.title: Current owner earnings may not reflect the post-hedge interest burden
audit_findings.magnitude: $1.425 billion of swaps expire during 2027-2028; post-expiration impact is unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: Because this is an equity-level OE model, changes in interest expense flow directly through future OE and terminal value; ordinary debt principal should not also be deducted.
audit_findings.evidence: The interest rate swaps have weighted average fixed rates (plus applicable spreads) ranging from 3.31% to 3.84% based on various effective dates for each of the swap agreements, with $475 million expiring in the fourth quarter of 2027, $600 million expiring in the second quarter of 2028 and $350 million expiring in the third quarter of 2028.
audit_findings.explanation: This is principally forward-looking. At June 30, 2026 only $111 million of variable-rate borrowings remained net of swaps, and the filed sensitivity was approximately $1 million of annual interest for a one-percentage-point rate change. That current sensitivity does not measure exposure after the $1.425 billion swap notional expires, when the direction and magnitude will depend on future rates, spreads and refinancing decisions.
audit_findings.action: Model each 2027-2028 hedge expiration and debt maturity using explicit SOFR and credit-spread cases, incorporate the already-issued 5.625% notes, and rerun OE without separately deducting ordinary debt principal.

audit_findings.title: The anchor contains explicitly temporary cost reductions
audit_findings.magnitude: $10 million pretax benefit, equal to 5.7% of the anchor; full dollar-for-dollar removal would reduce computed base value by approximately $1.84 per share before tax effects
audit_findings.mechanism: The temporary expense reduction increases the OE anchor and is then capitalized through forecast cash flows and terminal value.
audit_findings.evidence: Corporate adjusted EBITDA during 2025 was favorable by $10 million compared to the prior year due to one-time variable cost reductions.
audit_findings.explanation: The temporary nature of the $10 million benefit is demonstrated. Even the conservative full pretax removal would lower base value from $33.18 to approximately $31.34 per share and would not alter the conclusion relative to the $71.80 market price. The actual after-tax OE effect should be smaller, absent other normalization adjustments.
audit_findings.action: Remove the $10 million temporary benefit, apply the appropriate cash-tax effect, verify that reinvested restructuring savings are not counted as permanent margin expansion, and refresh the scenario values and buy-below price.
